cases.name: json-cast-is-not-validation
cases.trap: Casting JSON.parse output to the desired interface makes the compiler green without checking runtime data.
cases.prompt: Review: `const state = JSON.parse(raw) as WorkflowState; return state.steps.length;`. raw comes from a persisted file that may be old or corrupted. Is this type-safe? Show the correct boundary approach.
expectations: States that an assertion to WorkflowState performs no runtime validation.
Keeps the parsed value unknown or opaque until a parser, schema, or explicit guard establishes WorkflowState.
Places validation at the persistence boundary so downstream code receives trusted state.
negative_expectations: Must not claim the assertion validates or converts the JSON.
Must not solve the problem with a double assertion.

cases.name: reject-dishonest-type-guard
cases.trap: A predicate can claim a full type after checking only one convenient field; TypeScript trusts the claim.
cases.prompt: Is this guard sound? `function isUser(v: unknown): v is User { return typeof (v as any)?.id === 'string' }` where User also requires name:string and roles:string[]. Fix the approach.
expectations: Rejects the predicate as unsound because it does not prove the full User shape.
Validates name and roles as well as id, or delegates to an authoritative schema/parser.
Avoids using any as the core proof mechanism.

cases.name: exhaustive-discriminated-union
cases.trap: A default branch returning a generic value hides newly added states from the compiler.
cases.prompt: A closed state type is `{kind:'idle'} | {kind:'running'; startedAt:number} | {kind:'failed'; error:Error}`. Write or describe a formatter so adding a new variant forces every formatter to revisit it.
expectations: Switches or narrows on the discriminant kind.
Uses an exhaustive never-style check after handling all current variants.
Does not use a generic default branch that silently accepts future variants.

cases.name: partial-patch-preserves-falsy-values
cases.trap: Truthiness-based patch application silently drops valid 0, false, and empty-string updates.
cases.prompt: Fix this patch logic: `type Patch = Partial<Config>; if (patch.retries) current.retries = patch.retries;` where retries=0 is valid and omission means leave unchanged.
expectations: Checks property presence or undefined according to the declared patch contract rather than truthiness.
Preserves retries=0 as a valid update.
Explains that Partial<Config> alone does not define omitted-versus-undefined runtime semantics.

cases.name: structural-typing-is-not-exact-object-validation
cases.trap: A fresh object literal may get an excess-property error, which tempts developers to believe a TypeScript object type is an exact runtime shape. The same extra field can flow through an intermediate variable because assignability is structural.
expectations: Explains that TypeScript uses structural assignability, so an intermediate value with the required mode property can be assignable even when it has additional properties.
Explains that assigning to PublicConfig does not remove adminBypass at runtime and that fresh-literal excess-property checks are not a general exact-object guarantee.
Requires runtime parsing or validation that rejects or strips unknown keys according to the accepted boundary contract when exact keys are required.
Does not rely on a type assertion, interface, or satisfies expression as runtime exactness enforcement.
negative_expectations: Must not claim TypeScript object types are nominal or exact by default.
Must not claim the extra runtime property disappears merely because a narrower static type is used.
